title: "Key (Attention)"
description: "In attention mechanisms, the representation used to match and retrieve relevant information from a sequence."
term: "Key (Attention)"
letter: "K"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

In an attention mechanism, every item in a sequence can be turned into a key,
a value, and a query. The key tells the model what information an item contains,
while the query asks, “which items should I pay attention to?”

## Technical explanation

Transformer attention computes scores between a query vector and key vectors.
The attention score for a key $k_i$ and query $q$ is often a dot product or a
scaled dot product, followed by a softmax normalization. The resulting weights
are then applied to the value vectors, allowing the model to focus on the most
relevant parts of the input sequence.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

The key/value/query formulation is central to transformer models. It allows a
model to condition each output on the most relevant inputs, which is essential
for long-range dependencies, retrieval, and contextual reasoning across tokens.

## How it works

For a token representation, a model creates a query, a key, and a value using
learned projection matrices. It then evaluates similarity between the query and
all keys, normalizes those similarities, and combines the matching values.
This is the central mechanism behind self-attention and cross-attention.

## Practical example

In a sentence, when the model processes the word “it,” the query for “it” is
compared with the keys of previous tokens. If the model identifies that the
relevant token is “cat,” the value for “cat” contributes most strongly to the
updated representation of “it.”

## Common misconceptions

- Keys and values are not the same conceptual role; keys are used for matching, values hold content.
- Attention scores are not a memory lookup in a literal database sense, though the analogy is useful.
- The model learns these projections, so their meaning is not fixed by humans.
